answer: Latency-attested physical custody. Each identity must hold a hardware module at a registered site and answer challenges within a site-specific round-trip bound; the bound derives from measured network distance to a fixed beacon, so an operator cannot relay a single module across sites faster than light allows. Sites are verified by utility records and on-site inspection against local references—a tundra substation, a basalt quarry, a jetty terminal. Faking N identities costs N modules, N physical sites, and N inspection fees; one operator cannot multiplex them.
